hug-5-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-002.title: Food output and population indices
hug-5-4-002.description: Hypothetical region. Initially food output and population both have index 100. Later the food-output index is 150 and the population index 125. Each series uses its own initial value as the base.
hug-5-4-002.caption: Original synthetic indices, not quantities in tonnes or numbers of people. The ratio measures a relative aggregate output-per-person change, not access or diet quality.

hug-5-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-003.title: Scattered strips and consolidated holdings
hug-5-4-003.description: Hypothetical paired parcel sketch. Left, before: six alternating narrow strips labeled A1,B1,A2,B2,A3,B3. Right, after: one contiguous block A and one contiguous block B. A and B denote the same two holders in both panels.
hug-5-4-003.caption: Original schematic of spatial consolidation, not a real enclosure award. Before is on the left and after on the right. Equal schematic areas do not document historic compensation, common rights or household migration.
hug-5-4-003.unitLabel: Left: before; right: after. Letters identify holders.

hug-5-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-4-004.title: Matched planting-method trial
hug-5-4-004.description: Hypothetical matched plots of the same crop under the same soil and weather conditions. Broadcasting scatters 1000 viable seeds, with 600 plants established and 2.4 tonnes/hectare yield. Drill rows place 1000 seeds, with 800 plants established and 3.0 tonnes/hectare yield.
hug-5-4-004.caption: Original synthetic controlled comparison for understanding planting technology. A seed drill places seed in rows at regulated spacing/depth; actual outcomes vary with equipment, management and environment.

hug-5-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-5-001.title: Seed varieties under two management treatments
hug-5-5-001.description: Hypothetical controlled cereal trial. Low inputs yield 2.0 tonnes/hectare for traditional seed and 2.2 for improved seed. Reliable water plus suitable nutrients yield 3.0 and 5.0 respectively. Other conditions are held comparable.
hug-5-5-001.caption: Original synthetic trial; treatments illustrate complementarity rather than real measured cultivar performance. The combined treatment cannot isolate the effect of water from nutrients.

hug-5-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-5-002.title: Adoption of an introduced high-yield package
hug-5-5-002.description: Hypothetical adjacent farming districts. West has 80% of farms adopting, reliable irrigation and affordable credit. East has 25% adopting, less reliable irrigation and limited credit. Other possible differences have not been fully controlled.
hug-5-5-002.caption: Original synthetic field-note/map comparison, not a real national adoption map. District averages do not show that every household has the same access or results.

hug-5-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-5-003.title: Regional withdrawals with expanding irrigated area
hug-5-5-003.description: Hypothetical region: initially 10,000 irrigated hectares use 8000 cubic meters each, totaling 80 million cubic meters. Later 20,000 irrigated hectares use 5000 each, totaling 100 million. Water use per hectare falls while irrigated land expands.
hug-5-5-003.caption: Original synthetic annual irrigation withdrawals. The chart measures totals, not aquifer recharge, stored water or yield. Lower unit use does not alone establish lower total resource pressure.

hug-5-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-5-004.title: One farm’s output, price and annual costs
hug-5-5-004.description: Hypothetical one-hectare farm. Before adoption:2 tonnes, price 300 currency units/tonne, all annual production costs 200 units. After:4 tonnes, the same price 300, all annual costs 900. Compare net return as revenue minus the supplied costs.
hug-5-5-004.caption: Original synthetic accounting case. No inflation, taxes, household consumption or unlisted cost is to be added. This illustrates why harvest size and net return are distinct.

hug-5-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-6-001.title: Where two farms’ annual harvests go
hug-5-6-001.description: Hypothetical farm accounts. Farm A harvests 2000 kilograms, retains 1600 for household use and sells 400. Farm B harvests 1000 kilograms, retains 100 for household use and sells 900. No other destination is included.
hug-5-6-001.caption: Original synthetic output destinations, not real farm statistics. Orientation concerns the principal use of output; neither sales nor household consumption has to be entirely absent.

hug-5-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-6-002.title: Potential annual surplus before paying land rent
hug-5-6-002.description: Hypothetical activities on the same suitable one-hectare site. After all nonland costs, market gardening has 2000 currency units available, grain 400 and pasture 250. Annual rent for that site is 800 units.
hug-5-6-002.caption: Original synthetic single-site comparison. Surplus is revenue minus all nonland costs. Other sites, prices, technologies and crop suitability could change the ranking.

hug-5-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-6-003.title: Grain share of cultivated land by district
hug-5-6-003.description: Hypothetical crop-area survey: NW 80%, SW 70%, NE 30%, SE 20% of each district’s cropland is grain. All districts also grow other crops; total hectares and sales destinations are not supplied.
hug-5-6-003.caption: Original synthetic regional shares. The map summarizes crop concentration at district scale, not total grain tonnes, individual-field mixtures or household market dependence.
hug-5-6-003.unitLabel: Grain as a share of district cropland (%)

hug-5-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-6-004.title: Three-season records for four fields
hug-5-6-004.description: Hypothetical same-field planting records. A:maize/maize/maize; B:maize/beans/wheat; C:maize+beans together in each season; D:beans/beans/beans. A plus sign means crops share that field during the same season.
hug-5-6-004.caption: Original synthetic planting records. Field-level crop diversity and rotation describe different dimensions; neither alone identifies the farm’s sales destination.

hug-5-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-7-001.title: One grain-to-bread commodity chain
hug-5-7-001.description: Hypothetical chain: a farm sends grain to a mill, the mill sends flour to a bakery, and the bakery sends bread to a shop. Arrows describe product movements between linked stages, not money flows or quantities.
hug-5-7-001.caption: Original schematic. Milling and baking transform products; stages may be geographically separated. The question specifies no substitute flour supply or inventory.
hug-5-7-001.assumptions: Only the displayed suppliers are available; bakery flour inventory is zero.

hug-5-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-7-002.title: Equipment cost at two annual output levels
hug-5-7-002.description: Hypothetical same equipment and crop. Annual fixed cost 24000 currency units at either output; variable cost 40 units per tonne. Compare farms producing 200 and 1200 tonnes, both within the equipment’s usable capacity.
hug-5-7-002.caption: Original synthetic cost assumptions. Include both fixed and variable costs when computing average cost; this does not claim costs fall indefinitely beyond capacity.

hug-5-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-7-003.title: Operation counts and land per operation
hug-5-7-003.description: Hypothetical region with two nonoverlapping size groups and no unlisted farmland. Initially 200 small operations at 10 hectares each and 20 large at 100 each. Later 100 small at 10 each and 30 large at 100 each.
hug-5-7-003.caption: Original synthetic census comparison. Counts are not hectares; multiply by land per operation. Size labels do not establish ownership, crop choice or household migration.

hug-5-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-7-004.title: Separate accounts along one product chain
hug-5-7-004.description: Hypothetical accounts for stages handling the same final product batch. Receipts/all costs: farm 300/200, mill 900/800, bakery 1800/1600, retail 3000/2900 currency units. All costs include intermediate purchases and other costs of that stage.
hug-5-7-004.caption: Original synthetic accounting comparison. Each row is one stage’s account; do not add repeated intermediate sales as if they were distinct final products.

hug-5-8-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-8-001.title: Four zones around one market
hug-5-8-001.description: Hypothetical von Thünen-style schematic with central market M. Zones I,II,III,IV run from nearest to farthest. Their boundaries are concentric; the labels do not specify actual crop regions or measured distances.
hug-5-8-001.caption: Original idealized rings, not a real agricultural map. Zone widths are illustrative. Crop placement depends on competing returns and transport costs under the stated assumptions.
hug-5-8-001.assumptions: One isolated market; uniform suitable land; no preferred transport corridor; comparable routes in all directions.

hug-5-8-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-8-002.title: Two activities’ potential rent bids by distance
hug-5-8-002.description: Hypothetical annual surplus before land rent, in currency units/hectare. At 0,10,20 km, A has 1200,600,0; B has 600,500,400. Each line is assumed linear between the plotted distances.
hug-5-8-002.caption: Original synthetic bid curves. All production costs and market prices are held fixed; only distance-related delivery costs change. The greater positive surplus can support a higher bid for the same suitable site.

hug-5-8-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-8-003.title: Equal distances with different route costs
hug-5-8-003.description: Hypothetical uniform plain. A is 35 km west of market M; B 35 km east. Each ships one tonne to M. A’s corridor costs 2 currency units/tonne-km; B’s ordinary route costs 6. Arrows point toward the market.
hug-5-8-003.caption: Original schematic using 1 km per coordinate unit. The two routes are equally long but have different stated freight rates; no actual river, road or national border is mapped.

hug-5-8-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-8-004.title: Two buyers for the same farm product
hug-5-8-004.description: Hypothetical one-tonne sale. Market M1 is 10 km away and offers 100 currency units/tonne. M2 is 20 km away and offers 150. Production costs 40 units/tonne; freight costs 3 units/tonne-km to either market.
hug-5-8-004.caption: Original synthetic competing-market case. The farmer can choose either buyer with no unlisted costs; no claim is made about all farmers or actual city prices.

hug-5-9-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-9-001.title: Three countries in one agricultural product network
hug-5-9-001.description: Hypothetical countries A,B,C. Beans are grown in A, shipped to a processor in B, and processed products are shipped from B to consumers in C. Arrows show product directions rather than money or tonnage.
hug-5-9-001.caption: Original international-network schematic, not a world map or real trade route. Country shapes, labels and activities are invented for the exercise.

hug-5-9-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-9-002.title: Export earnings before a coffee-price shock
hug-5-9-002.description: Hypothetical annual export revenues in million currency units. X:coffee 80, other exports 20. Y:coffee 40, other exports 160. Only coffee prices change in the question; volumes and other earnings remain fixed.
hug-5-9-002.caption: Original synthetic concentration comparison. Coffee earnings are one component of total exports; the table does not describe complete national production or household outcomes.

hug-5-9-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-9-003.title: One grain’s annual production and trade account
hug-5-9-003.description: Hypothetical annual grain account, all in thousand tonnes:domestic production 80, imports 40, exports 10, losses 20. No stock changes, seed, feed or other unlisted uses occur in this exercise.
hug-5-9-003.caption: Original synthetic flows. Bars are positive magnitudes; decide which add to and which subtract from domestic food availability. This is not a household-access measure.

hug-5-9-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-9-004.title: Two hypothetical import offers
hug-5-9-004.description: Hypothetical per-tonne offers in currency units. Near:product price 100, freight 10, import duty 30. Far:price 90, freight 30, duty 0. No other cost or restriction applies.
hug-5-9-004.caption: Original sourcing exercise. Duties are invented fixed amounts per tonne, not percentages or current government policies. Add all three components for landed cost.

hug-5-10-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-10-001.title: Annual salt inputs and drainage losses
hug-5-10-001.description: Hypothetical irrigated area. Water brings 100 tonnes of dissolved salts into the soil during a year; drainage removes 30 tonnes. There are no other salt inputs or outputs in this exercise.
hug-5-10-001.caption: Original synthetic salt budget, not a water-volume balance. Initial salt stock and soil mass are unspecified, so calculate the stock change rather than a final concentration or crop loss.

hug-5-10-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-10-002.title: Sediment loss in a matched rainfall trial
hug-5-10-002.description: Hypothetical matched plots with comparable slope, soil and applied rainfall. Measured sediment loss:bare soil 40 tonnes/hectare, continuous cover 10, maintained terraces 8. Treatments differ in surface management.
hug-5-10-002.caption: Original synthetic trial, not measured outcomes at a real farm. Sediment leaving a plot is not the same measure as crop yield, runoff volume or downstream damage.

hug-5-10-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-10-003.title: Wetland conversion in a before-and-after plan
hug-5-10-003.description: Hypothetical same site shown before on the left and after on the right. Before:a wetland with recorded seasonal water-storage and habitat functions. After:drained cropland with a ditch leading to an outlet. Panels are schematics of the same place, not adjacent properties.
hug-5-10-003.caption: Original land-cover change sketch. The arrow indicates drainage toward an outlet. Cultivated area, hydrologic effects, habitat conditions and actual crop returns require separate measurements.

hug-5-10-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-10-004.title: Daily work hours in one farming community
hug-5-10-004.description: Hypothetical group-average daily hours before and after commercial-crop expansion. Women:paid 3→7, unpaid 6→6. Men:paid 5→7, unpaid 2→2. Categories are separate and do not overlap.
hug-5-10-004.caption: Original synthetic time-use data. The comparison records workloads, not income control, wages or all causes of the change; group averages do not describe every individual.

hug-5-11-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-11-001.title: Yield response to one target-insect-resistant trait
hug-5-11-001.description: Hypothetical matched trial of otherwise comparable crop lines. With high target-insect pressure:conventional yield 3, resistant yield 5 tonnes/hectare. Without that insect:both yield 5. Other trial conditions are matched within each location.
hug-5-11-001.caption: Original synthetic trait/context comparison. The graph measures yield, not all costs, pesticide use, biodiversity effects or food safety. No actual cultivar is represented.

hug-5-11-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-11-002.title: Travel time to a full-service food store
hug-5-11-002.description: Hypothetical district medians for a one-way trip:West 10 minutes, Central 50, East 20. Recorded household incomes and food prices are comparable for this exercise. Other aspects of access are not fully measured.
hug-5-11-002.caption: Original synthetic screening map. Store type and trip definition are held consistent; medians can hide within-district variation, and the map alone does not establish every resident’s food security.

hug-5-11-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-11-003.title: Two direct-sale arrangements
hug-5-11-003.description: Hypothetical farm offers. A:members pay 300 currency units before planting and receive a season’s harvest share, whose quantity varies with the harvest. B:buyers pay for individual purchases on delivery with no preseason payment.
hug-5-11-003.caption: Original terms for comparing cash timing and shared production risk. Neither arrangement promises a particular profit, identical food value or affordability for every household.

hug-5-11-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-11-004.title: Two aquaculture systems with equal fish output
hug-5-11-004.description: Hypothetical annual systems comparison. A:fish output 10 tonnes, feed 20 tonnes, measured nutrient discharge 100 kg. B:fish output 10 tonnes, feed 12 tonnes, nutrient discharge 40 kg.
hug-5-11-004.caption: Original synthetic efficiency/discharge data. The nutrient is measured consistently between systems; unlisted outcomes remain unknown. Ratios compare feed and output in the same mass unit.

hug-5-12-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-12-001.title: Work participation and registered ownership records
hug-5-12-001.description: Hypothetical community. Agricultural-worker record:women 90, men 60. Registered-landowner record:women 10, men 40. Each row is a separate complete record; individual links and land areas are not supplied.
hug-5-12-001.caption: Original synthetic data. A worker may or may not be a registered owner. Registration is not a complete measure of all use rights, management or control of earnings.

hug-5-12-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-12-002.title: Recorded workers in three agrifood roles
hug-5-12-002.description: Hypothetical task survey. Planting:women 60, men 40. Packing:women 10, men 90. Selling:women 80, men 20. Each role has 100 recorded workers; a person may be counted in more than one role.
hug-5-12-002.caption: Original synthetic participation counts. Compare roles separately; do not add them to estimate unique people or infer wages, ownership or decision-making.

hug-5-12-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-12-003.title: Applications and approvals for one farm-credit program
hug-5-12-003.description: Hypothetical program records:women 80 applicants and 40 approvals; men 20 applicants and 15 approvals. Every approval belongs to a listed applicant. Other applicant and loan characteristics are not provided.
hug-5-12-003.caption: Original synthetic aggregate outcomes. Rates use applicants as denominators; the table alone does not explain why an application was approved or denied.

hug-5-12-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-5-12-004.title: Women-managed operations in four production districts
hug-5-12-004.description: Hypothetical survey:NW 65%, NE 55%, SW 25%, SE 35% of agricultural operations are women-managed. Northern districts specialize in market gardening; southern districts in grain. Other regional conditions may also differ.
hug-5-12-004.caption: Original synthetic production-region comparison. Management, ownership and labor participation are separate categories. District percentages do not identify every resident’s role or establish why the pattern occurs.

hug-6-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-1-001.title: Local setting and connections at settlement P
hug-6-1-001.description: Hypothetical coastal setting. P is beside a river mouth and inlet; field notes identify deep sheltered water and near-level ground there. A road links P with an inland settlement. Coastline shape alone does not establish water depth.
hug-6-1-001.caption: Original schematic. Local terrain/water observations describe the site; connections with other settlements describe situation. No real port, navigability survey or growth forecast is represented.

hug-6-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-1-002.title: Components of recorded urban population change
hug-6-1-002.description: Hypothetical urban population ledger starting at 100,000. Births 3000; deaths 1000; arrivals 6000; departures 2000; another 2000 residents are reclassified as urban. The reclassified group has not moved and is not included in the other entries.
hug-6-1-002.caption: Original synthetic accounting example. Reclassification changes an urban category’s count rather than necessarily creating physical migration. No other change occurs in this exercise.

hug-6-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-1-003.title: Urban and rural populations in two periods
hug-6-1-003.description: Hypothetical national population, thousands of people. Initial:urban 100, rural 100. Later:urban 120, rural 180. Urban/rural classifications remain consistent between periods.
hug-6-1-003.caption: Original synthetic counts. A change in urban population is not automatically a change in its share of the country’s population; use both categories for the denominator.

hug-6-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-1-004.title: Hub travel times before and after a transport project
hug-6-1-004.description: Hypothetical unchanged settlement sites P and Q connect to a regional hub. P’s journey changes 60→20 minutes; Q’s remains 30→30. Arrows indicate trips toward the hub, not population migration.
hug-6-1-004.caption: Original accessibility schematic; line length is not travel time. The project changes connections rather than the physical location or local soil of either settlement.
hug-6-1-004.assumptions: Compare the same trip definition and hub before/after; other connections and settlement sites remain unchanged.

hug-6-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-2-001.title: Three hypothetical urban agglomerations
hug-6-2-001.description: Hypothetical populations measured in the same year using comparable agglomeration boundaries:A 8.5 million, B 12 million, C 22 million. The question supplies the population thresholds to apply.
hug-6-2-001.caption: Original synthetic city counts, not current city rankings. Size categories are not automatically measures of global economic influence, wealth or service quality.

hug-6-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-2-002.title: Different forms beyond an established urban core
hug-6-2-002.description: Hypothetical region. The old core is near the west. X is a large new office/retail job concentration on formerly rural land; E is a mainly residential far-outer settlement with commuting ties across intervening open land.
hug-6-2-002.caption: Original schematic. Roles come from field records, not a population inferred from point size. Edge-city-type centers and exurban settlements describe different functions and spatial relationships.
hug-6-2-002.unitLabel: Core:old center; X:job/retail cluster; E:far-outer homes

hug-6-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-2-003.title: Residents in the center and outer municipalities
hug-6-2-003.description: Hypothetical metropolitan population, millions. Initial:center 1.0, outer municipalities 1.0. Later:center 1.1, outer municipalities 2.0. Boundaries and component definitions stay constant.
hug-6-2-003.caption: Original synthetic within-metro counts. Resident distribution does not directly measure jobs, household origins, travel mode or individual migration routes.

hug-6-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-2-004.title: Compact and separated development patterns
hug-6-2-004.description: Hypothetical alternative development sketches. Left:C is one compact block. Right:X,Y,Z are separate developed patches with open spaces between. The panels illustrate arrangement, not actual cities or measured commuting routes.
hug-6-2-004.caption: Original schematic contrast. Open land is the unfilled space; the letters identify developed patches. Fragmentation can raise infrastructure and land-use questions, but actual costs and travel modes require evidence.

hug-6-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-3-001.title: Population and selected international business functions
hug-6-3-001.description: Hypothetical city records. A:4 million residents,120 multinational headquarters,150 connected overseas offices. B:18 million residents,10 headquarters,20 connected offices. Indicators are illustrative, not an official ranking formula.
hug-6-3-001.caption: Original synthetic comparison. Corporate functions, network integration and population are different dimensions; headquarters counts alone are not a complete measure of urban importance.

hug-6-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-3-002.title: A city coordinating activities in other cities
hug-6-3-002.description: Hypothetical cities in different countries. H coordinates financing, legal services and production information with A,B,C. Arrows show the supplied coordination links, not measured worker migration or equality of power.
hug-6-3-002.caption: Original network schematic. Organizational and service connections can join distant cities. The graph is a selected example, not a full world-city hierarchy or quantified flow model.
hug-6-3-002.assumptions: Links identify functions in the field records; unshown links may exist and geometric line length is not distance.

hug-6-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-3-003.title: Near and distant service-contract links
hug-6-3-003.description: Hypothetical selected contracts:A–B 3 annually, A–C 30. A and B lie in one country and C in another; C is farther from A in the schematic. Arrows indicate the recorded direction of service contracting.
hug-6-3-003.caption: Original schematic, not a real geography or complete count of interaction. Contract number does not directly measure financial value, worker flows or the cause of a relationship.

hug-6-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-3-004.title: Four observations of urban activities
hug-6-3-004.description: Hypothetical field records for one city. The task is to identify an explicitly recorded cross-border cultural connection rather than infer it from population or headquarters counts.
hug-6-3-004.caption: Original invented source notes. A local record may have wider context that is not shown; judge what each observation directly establishes.
rows: Bus trips between neighborhoods in the same city
City producers collaborate with performance venues in another country
Refuse collection serving one residential block

hug-6-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-4-001.title: Populations in one hypothetical urban hierarchy
hug-6-4-001.description: Hypothetical same-year urban agglomerations using comparable boundaries. Ranked populations are 12,3,2,1 million. The largest is four times the second-largest.
hug-6-4-001.caption: Original synthetic population distribution. Use the simple rank-size benchmark P(r)=P(1)/r for comparison; the chart does not identify the causes of the observed hierarchy.

hug-6-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-4-002.title: An ideal rank-size model with one missing value
hug-6-4-002.description: Hypothetical model hierarchy with largest city 12 million. Rank two is 6 million, rank three is missing, and rank four is 3 million. Apply P(r)=P(1)/r, with consistent population units.
hug-6-4-002.caption: Original model exercise, not an observed country. Rank is an ordering number, not a distance or administrative level.

hug-6-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-4-003.title: Destination size and distance from one origin
hug-6-4-003.description: Hypothetical destinations. A has 100,000 residents at 10 km; B has 200,000 at 20 km. For this exercise compare P(destination)/distance², holding origin size and all other model terms fixed.
hug-6-4-003.caption: Original gravity-style index exercise. Distance is in the same unit for both routes. The index is not an observed number of trips and does not include every influence on interaction.

hug-6-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-4-004.title: Local markets and one higher-order service center
hug-6-4-004.description: Hypothetical uniform region with seven local market areas. Each center, H and A–F, has a grocer. H also has a specialty service requiring more customers than one local area supplies. Hexagons are an idealized coverage pattern, not real boundaries.
hug-6-4-004.caption: Original central-place-style schematic. Higher-order demand draws across local areas; this does not assign an exact historical K-order or universal service geography. Dots locate centers, not resident counts.
hug-6-4-004.unitLabel: Each dot:local grocer. H:also a specialty service.

hug-6-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-5-001.title: A concentric internal-city abstraction
hug-6-5-001.description: Hypothetical teaching diagram inspired by the Burgess model. The CBD is central; II is a transition zone, III and IV residential zones, and V an outer commuting zone. These are stylized land-use bands, not observed neighborhoods.
hug-6-5-001.caption: Original nested polygons approximate circles without copying a published figure. Historical model categories do not determine the wealth, identity or conditions of every present-day resident.

hug-6-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-5-002.title: Selected urban sectors along directional corridors
hug-6-5-002.description: Hypothetical Hoyt-style example. A is a residential sector extending along an amenity/access corridor; B is an industrial sector along rail access. Both extend outward from the CBD. Only selected sectors are shown.
hug-6-5-002.caption: Original schematic, not a real city. Sector shape illustrates directionality; it does not imply all actual cities or income groups follow fixed wedges.

hug-6-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-5-003.title: Distinct functional clusters within one urban region
hug-6-5-003.description: Hypothetical urban plan with an older CBD, a separate retail center and an industrial cluster near specialized freight access. Field records link their separation to different site needs and incompatibility of some activities.
hug-6-5-003.caption: Original selected-cluster schematic. Blank space is not a complete land-use inventory; multiple-nuclei reasoning does not imply all clusters have equal power, population or independence.
hug-6-5-003.unitLabel: Three distinct activity clusters, not three separate cities

hug-6-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-5-004.title: Selected features considered in regional urban models
hug-6-5-004.description: Hypothetical model-comparison notes. They highlight selected historical relationships rather than classify all actual cities or residents in a region.
hug-6-5-004.caption: Original summary of model questions, not copied diagrams or an exhaustive regional typology. Apply each with local evidence and attention to subsequent change.
rows: A commercial spine extending the CBD, with a related higher-cost residential sector
Historic port functions and associated commercial activities shaping internal organization
Local and colonial histories contributing different business districts and settlement forms

hug-6-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-6-001.title: Dwelling units and residential land area
hug-6-6-001.description: Hypothetical districts. A contains 200 dwelling units on 10 residential hectares; B contains 100 units on 2 residential hectares. Areas refer to residential land under the same definition.
hug-6-6-001.caption: Original synthetic housing-stock data. Dwelling units are not resident counts; identical housing-unit density would not require identical household sizes or occupancy.

hug-6-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-6-002.title: A vacant urban parcel before and after infill
hug-6-6-002.description: Hypothetical same urban site in two panels. Left before:a vacant parcel lies between existing north/south buildings. Right after:new homes occupy that parcel; the urban edge and neighboring buildings are unchanged.
hug-6-6-002.caption: Original paired-site schematic, not adjacent neighborhoods. Labels identify existing buildings and the changed parcel. The drawing does not specify rents, tenure or individual household outcomes.
hug-6-6-002.unitLabel: Left:before. Right:after. Outer boxes:unchanged urban edge.

hug-6-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-6-003.title: Housing stock by building type in two periods
hug-6-6-003.description: Hypothetical dwelling-unit counts. Initial:detached 600, attached 200, apartments 200. Later:detached 500, attached 300, apartments 700. Categories do not overlap; the chart counts units rather than people.
hug-6-6-003.caption: Original synthetic housing mix. Type can relate to land-use intensity, but unit totals alone do not establish exact land area, occupancy, rents or resident characteristics.

hug-6-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-6-004.title: Same population, different land-area definitions
hug-6-6-004.description: Hypothetical districts A and B each contain 1000 residents on 10 total hectares. A has 5 residential hectares; B has 2. All residents live within the designated residential area, and the remaining land has other uses.
hug-6-6-004.caption: Original synthetic density comparison. The question explicitly defines gross and net measures; different agencies may use other boundaries, so do not compare unlabeled densities.

hug-6-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-7-001.title: Households connected to the water network
hug-6-7-001.description: Hypothetical neighboring districts: West 90% and East 40% of households have a water-network connection. The map records connections, not service reliability or water consumption.
hug-6-7-001.caption: Original synthetic access rates. District sizes on this schematic do not represent household totals. Investigating unequal access also requires investment histories and local evidence.

hug-6-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-7-002.title: Jobs reachable within a transit travel-time threshold
hug-6-7-002.description: Hypothetical residents of districts A and B. Each count is jobs reachable within 45 minutes by transit. The same regional job inventory and counting method are used before and after a network change.
hug-6-7-002.caption: Original accessibility counts, not employment gains. Schedules, transfers and routes can change reachable opportunities even when the job inventory is held constant.

hug-6-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-7-003.title: Monthly service interruptions despite full coverage
hug-6-7-003.description: Hypothetical water-network districts. All households are connected in both years. Values are average monthly hours without service, measured with the same method: A 12 then 3, B 4 then 4.
hug-6-7-003.caption: Original quality-of-service data. Fewer outage hours represent greater reliability on this measure; no cause, outage-event count or water-quality result is specified.

hug-6-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-7-004.title: A citywide service-capacity account
hug-6-7-004.description: Hypothetical planning account using the same abstract daily capacity unit for both entries. Existing capacity is usable under the scenario; projected need is for the same service and date.
hug-6-7-004.caption: Original simplified comparison. Capacity totals do not locate network branches, determine household connection prices or provide engineering design guidance.

hug-6-8-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-8-001.title: Straight-line proximity and usable walking routes
hug-6-8-001.description: Hypothetical neighborhood plans. The same home-to-shop comparison is measured in each. Route length follows a legal pedestrian connection, including required crossings; straight-line distance ignores the street network.
hug-6-8-001.caption: Original design comparison. A short usable route can support walkability, but surface conditions, crossings, accessibility and safety also need evaluation.

hug-6-8-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-8-002.title: A mixed-use station-area proposal
hug-6-8-002.description: Hypothetical plan with homes west of a station and shops east of it. A continuous pedestrian route links the three. All parcels shown are within the proposed station-area district; no real city or measured travel-time radius is represented.
hug-6-8-002.caption: Original schematic of land-use and access relationships. Physical design does not establish prices, accessibility for every user, service frequency or actual travel behavior.
hug-6-8-002.unitLabel: Homes + shops + pedestrian access to transit

hug-6-8-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-8-003.title: Travel intensity and a changing city population
hug-6-8-003.description: Hypothetical city in two periods. Vehicle travel includes all motor-vehicle kilometers allocated per resident using the same accounting method. Values are not emissions measurements.
hug-6-8-003.caption: Original planning indicators. Per-person and total outcomes may move in different directions when population changes; the figures alone do not identify a policy’s causal effect.

hug-6-8-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-8-004.title: Two indicators following a neighborhood redesign
hug-6-8-004.description: Hypothetical comparable neighborhood observations before and after redesign: walking share among surveyed local trips and median monthly asking rent. No control neighborhood or household-income observations are provided.
hug-6-8-004.caption: Original synthetic indicators. A median asking rent is not every existing tenant’s rent, and a before/after association does not isolate the cause of a change.

hug-6-9-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-9-001.title: Population counts and age composition
hug-6-9-001.description: Hypothetical urban district with unchanged boundaries and the same under-18 definition in both censuses. Counts include all residents under the stated enumeration method.
hug-6-9-001.caption: Original synthetic census-style observations. An increase in a group’s count need not mean an increase in its share, and age alone does not identify every household type.

hug-6-9-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-9-002.title: Selected residents describe a changing district
hug-6-9-002.description: Hypothetical field notes written for this question, not real quotations. Two selected participants discuss a recent station-area redevelopment; they were not chosen as a representative survey.
hug-6-9-002.caption: Original fictional accounts. Narrative evidence can reveal meanings and mechanisms while leaving the prevalence of each view uncertain.
rows: The new walking connection makes the shops easier for me to reach.
I welcome the connection but worry about rising housing costs.

hug-6-9-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-9-003.title: Population change within fixed urban districts
hug-6-9-003.description: Hypothetical census counts at equal five-year intervals. Inner: 1000, 1100, 1200. Outer: 1000, 1500, 2000. District definitions and enumeration methods remain unchanged.
hug-6-9-003.caption: Original synthetic time series. Lines connect census observations and do not imply observations for each intervening year or a particular cause of change.

hug-6-9-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-9-004.title: Two surveys about one redevelopment plan
hug-6-9-004.description: Hypothetical surveys. Station respondents volunteered at one station. The city survey used a probability sample of city residents with suitable geographic coverage; neither result is a census.
hug-6-9-004.caption: Original sample records. Assess target population, recruitment, wording and nonresponse as well as sample size when evaluating urban attitudes.

hug-6-10-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-10-001.title: Two hypothetical household housing budgets
hug-6-10-001.description: Hypothetical households using the same currency and monthly net-income definition. A: income 2000, rent 600. B: income 2500, rent 900. No other spending or household-size data are supplied.
hug-6-10-001.caption: Original budget comparison for a geographic affordability indicator. It is not financial advice or an eligibility determination; costs and household needs require more context.

hug-6-10-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-10-002.title: Tracking an original household cohort after redevelopment
hug-6-10-002.description: Hypothetical linked records follow the same 1000 original households. At follow-up 600 remain in the neighborhood. Treat each original household as one tracked unit; no splitting or merging occurs in this simplified account.
hug-6-10-002.caption: Original cohort illustration. Records identify presence, not moving reasons, coercion, destinations or the number of newly arriving households.

hug-6-10-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-10-003.title: Unequal modeled exposure in neighboring districts
hug-6-10-003.description: Hypothetical districts. A has a modeled exposure index of 70 and lower average household income than B; B has an index of 20. Higher index means more modeled exposure on the same 0–100 scale. No actual pollutant or health threshold is represented.
hug-6-10-003.caption: Original synthetic disparity map. It supports a question about environmental burdens, not individual health, every household’s income or a proven historical cause.

hug-6-10-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-10-004.title: A fictional inclusionary housing requirement
hug-6-10-004.description: Hypothetical project rule written for this question. It requires 20% of all new dwellings to satisfy the rule’s affordability condition. The project contains 150 new dwellings, with no exemptions or rounding issues.
hug-6-10-004.caption: Original policy arithmetic, not a real regulation or advice about compliance. Eligibility, prices, duration and enforcement are not specified.

hug-6-11-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-11-001.title: Urban land consumption and population growth
hug-6-11-001.description: Hypothetical metropolitan region. Urbanized land is measured by the same built-area definition in both periods, and population refers to that land. Regional administrative boundaries do not change.
hug-6-11-001.caption: Original synthetic footprint indicators. Built land per resident is one measure of land consumption, not the complete ecological footprint of goods and resources consumed elsewhere.

hug-6-11-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-11-002.title: Parcel histories for a redevelopment discussion
hug-6-11-002.description: Hypothetical site records. A is a disused industrial parcel inside the urban area with possible contamination. B is never-developed farmland outside it. C is an occupied shop with no reported reuse barrier; absence of a report is not a safety certification.
hug-6-11-002.caption: Original fictional inventory. Prior use and potential contamination are reasons for site-specific investigation, not a medical risk estimate or permission to occupy land.
rows: Operating shop; no reported reuse barrier

hug-6-11-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-11-003.title: Energy use by sector in two periods
hug-6-11-003.description: Hypothetical city energy account. Initial: housing 30, industry 50, transport 20 units. Later: housing 25, industry 35, transport 40. Categories do not overlap, and the same accounting boundary and energy unit are used.
hug-6-11-003.caption: Original synthetic energy data. The account measures consumption, not emissions, population, industrial output or the life-cycle footprint of all imported goods.

hug-6-11-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-6-11-004.title: New building additions inside and beyond a growth boundary
hug-6-11-004.description: Hypothetical regional monitoring. Counts are new buildings added in each observation year, inside and beyond one designated urban growth boundary. Boundaries and counting methods are fixed; no control region is supplied.
hug-6-11-004.caption: Original synthetic regional data. Building counts do not measure occupied households, parcel area, displacement or policy causation.

hug-7-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-1-001.title: Fuel and transport in a fictional industrial district
hug-7-1-001.description: Hypothetical early-industrial district. A coal source and mill are connected to a canal corridor. The map illustrates possible location advantages, not an actual historical town or a sufficient explanation of industrialization.
hug-7-1-001.caption: Original schematic. Capital, labor, institutions, markets and technology are not measured by the drawing; the canal is a transport connection rather than a claim about the mill’s power source.

hug-7-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-1-002.title: Production before and after mechanization
hug-7-1-002.description: Hypothetical workshop producing the same standardized product in equal observation periods. Both periods use 100 workers and the same total working hours; output changes from 1000 to 3000 units.
hug-7-1-002.caption: Original synthetic productivity account. It illustrates output per worker, not actual historical statistics, a wage record or proof that technology always increases employment.

hug-7-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-1-003.title: An expanding workforce and changing sector shares
hug-7-1-003.description: Hypothetical region. Sector categories are mutually exclusive and cover all workers. Initial total 1000; later total 2000. Entries are employment percentages rather than output values.
hug-7-1-003.caption: Original synthetic structural-change data. Composition changes do not by themselves follow individual workers or identify causes of workforce growth.

hug-7-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-1-004.title: Material and market links in an imperial trading system
hug-7-1-004.description: Hypothetical industrial-era imperial system: R is a raw-material region, F a metropolitan manufacturing center and M a colonial market. Arrows show R supplying cotton to F and F selling cloth to M. Political control is part of the scenario, not inferred solely from arrow direction.
hug-7-1-004.caption: Original simplified network. Colonial relationships were unequal and varied; this is one industrial economic motive, not a universal history of all trade or imperialism.
hug-7-1-004.assumptions: R supplies material; F manufactures; M buys cloth. Links indicate functions, not equal gains or flow quantities.

hug-7-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-2-001.title: Transport, labor and clustering savings at three sites
hug-7-2-001.description: Hypothetical manufacturer making the same output each day at A, B or C. Cost units are comparable. Daily total = transport + labor − agglomeration savings. All omitted costs are assumed equal.
hug-7-2-001.caption: Original simplified least-cost comparison. Agglomeration can reduce some costs, but actual clustering may also bring congestion or other disadvantages not included here.

hug-7-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-2-002.title: One source, one market and a weight-losing process
hug-7-2-002.description: Hypothetical batch: 3 tons of localized input at S yield 1 ton of finished product sold at M. The route is 100 km and freight costs 2 units per ton-km. Consider a plant either at S or M; local movement costs zero and all other costs are equal.
hug-7-2-002.caption: Original two-location transport model. A given shipping rate and weight change do not describe every real industry or account for all location factors.
hug-7-2-002.assumptions: S is the sole input source; M is the sole market. Plant choices are S or M only. One batch, uniform rate, no intermediate input or product trips.

hug-7-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-2-003.title: Broad employment sectors in two fictional regions
hug-7-2-003.description: Hypothetical shares of all employed workers. A: primary 60%, secondary 25%, services 15%. B: primary 15%, secondary 30%, services 55%. Broad services include tertiary and higher-order service activities in this three-part account.
hug-7-2-003.caption: Original synthetic shares. Employment percentages do not directly measure sector output, productivity, wages, job quality or a complete level of development.

hug-7-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-2-004.title: A ship-to-rail freight connection
hug-7-2-004.description: Hypothetical coast and cargo route. Sea is west, land east. A ship route reaches port P; cargo transfers to rail and continues to inland F. Arrows show shipment direction rather than flow volume.
hug-7-2-004.caption: Original schematic. Transfer can occur without unpacking each container or processing goods at the port; no actual route, distance or population is represented.
hug-7-2-004.unitLabel: Ship → port P → rail → inland F

hug-7-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-3-001.title: Domestic production and residents’ national income
hug-7-3-001.description: Hypothetical economy in one year. GDP and net primary income are in billions of the same currency; population is in millions. Net primary income from abroad can be negative. Use the stated GNI identity, converting billions to millions before dividing.
hug-7-3-001.caption: Original simplified national accounts. Per-resident GNI is an average of residents’ aggregate income, not a household wage, distribution measure or financial recommendation.
rows: Net primary income from abroad (billion currency)

hug-7-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-3-002.title: Equal means and different income distributions
hug-7-3-002.description: Hypothetical groups of four households, with comparable household sizes and income definitions. Entries are total income in the same currency and period. This is not a national sample.
hug-7-3-002.caption: Original synthetic distribution example. Average income is useful but can conceal differences among households; no real household is represented.

hug-7-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-3-003.title: Contrasting human-development dimensions
hug-7-3-003.description: Hypothetical economies. Life expectancy is at birth; mean schooling refers to adults and expected schooling to children entering school. Income is comparable GNI per capita in purchasing-power units. No normalized indices or composite formula are provided.
hug-7-3-003.caption: Original synthetic indicators, not real-country values. HDI summarizes selected average dimensions and does not include every environmental, political or distributional condition.

hug-7-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-3-004.title: A hypothetical gender-inequality index pattern
hug-7-3-004.description: Hypothetical comparable regional GII values: NW 0.2, NE 0.3, SW 0.6, SE 0.7. Lower GII indicates lower measured gender inequality; the index summarizes reproductive health, empowerment and labor-market dimensions.
hug-7-3-004.caption: Original synthetic index map. These are not real regional estimates and cannot identify each resident’s income, identity or opportunities.

hug-7-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-4-001.title: Working-age population and labor-force participation
hug-7-4-001.description: Hypothetical labor statistics using two reported categories. Labor force includes employed and qualifying unemployed jobseekers; working age and jobseeking definitions are the same across groups.
hug-7-4-001.caption: Original synthetic data. The table does not capture all gender identities, unpaid care, job quality or equal opportunity; those require additional evidence.

hug-7-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-4-002.title: Comparable average hourly earnings over time
hug-7-4-002.description: Hypothetical reported averages in the same price-adjusted currency. Women: 80 then 90; men: 100 then 100. Categories and hourly-earnings definitions stay the same; occupational composition is not controlled.
hug-7-4-002.caption: Original synthetic earnings comparison. An unadjusted group average does not establish pay for identical work, the experience of every worker or the sole cause of a gap.

hug-7-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-4-003.title: Reported unpaid-care time in a fictional community
hug-7-4-003.description: Hypothetical comparable time-use survey. Average weekly unpaid-care hours are 20 for women and 10 for men in the reported categories. These are not total weekly hours of work or a complete account of every identity and task.
hug-7-4-003.caption: Original synthetic group averages. Unpaid work has economic and social significance even when it is absent from paid-employment counts.

hug-7-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-4-004.title: Observed incomes in a microenterprise-loan study
hug-7-4-004.description: Hypothetical women-led microenterprises. Groups had the same initial average but loan participation was not randomly assigned. Values are comparable monthly net enterprise income after stated business expenses; no individual records are shown.
hug-7-4-004.caption: Original synthetic evaluation data. Group averages do not guarantee loan benefits, identify causes or describe repayment risk for a real borrower.

hug-7-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-5-001.title: Five stages in a stylized growth framework
hug-7-5-001.description: Hypothetical teaching diagram of Rostow’s sequence. I: traditional society; II: preconditions for take-off; III: take-off; IV: drive to maturity; V: high mass consumption. Numbers are model stages, not years or measures of human worth.
hug-7-5-001.caption: Original diagram, not a copied historical figure. The sequence is a theoretical generalization with limits; contemporary societies should not be assumed to fit it perfectly.
hug-7-5-001.assumptions: Arrows indicate the proposed stage order only. Real development paths can differ, and historical/global relationships require additional analysis.

hug-7-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-5-002.title: Three fictional positions in a production system
hug-7-5-002.description: Hypothetical roles for analyzing a world-system. These summaries describe dominant relationships, not every firm or resident in a territory.
hug-7-5-002.caption: Original functional comparison. Core, semiperiphery and periphery are relational and historically changeable; no real country is assigned a fixed status.
rows: Major finance and design control; strong influence over production networks
Substantial manufacturing and some control functions; dependence on external finance or technology remains
Raw-material supply with limited control over major buyers and prices

hug-7-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-5-003.title: Export composition and commodity-price exposure
hug-7-5-003.description: Hypothetical economies with initial merchandise-export earnings of 100 currency units each. A: commodity exports 80, other exports 20. B: commodities 20, other exports 80. Consider only the stated common commodity-price shock.
hug-7-5-003.caption: Original synthetic export account. A larger commodity share can increase vulnerability to those prices; actual outcomes also depend on volumes, buffers, contracts and the wider economy.

hug-7-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-5-004.title: Two interpretations of uneven development
hug-7-5-004.description: Hypothetical analysts’ summaries written for this question. R studies a sequence of investment and production changes. D studies how external ownership, unequal bargaining and historical ties constrain development options.
hug-7-5-004.caption: Original comparative interpretations, not attributed quotations. Theoretical emphasis is not proof that all other factors are absent.
rows: Internal structural changes supporting a proposed sequence of growth
External control and unequal relationships shaping domestic opportunities

hug-7-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-6-001.title: Alternative outputs from one labor-day
hug-7-6-001.description: Hypothetical economies. With one labor-day A can make either 12 grain units or 6 cloth units; B either 4 grain or 4 cloth. Assume constant linear tradeoffs and transferable labor within each economy, ignoring trade costs.
hug-7-6-001.caption: Original production possibilities, not simultaneous output of both goods. Opportunity cost compares forgone alternative production; no current country or policy is represented.

hug-7-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-6-002.title: A fictional import-charge calculation
hug-7-6-002.description: Hypothetical rule: a 10% tariff applies to an import value of 100 currency units. Assume the full charge is passed to the buyer and that transport, exchange rates and all other charges or prices stay unchanged.
hug-7-6-002.caption: Original simplified example, not a current tariff, customs classification, legal instruction or prediction of actual pass-through.

hug-7-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-6-003.title: A cross-border component and assembly network
hug-7-6-003.description: Hypothetical economies: S supplies a required component, A assembles the finished product, M is the final market. There is no alternative source for the component within the scenario. Arrows show the stated shipment chain.
hug-7-6-003.caption: Original functional network. Actual firms can diversify or adapt; the no-substitute condition is an explicit teaching assumption rather than a claim about all supply chains.
hug-7-6-003.assumptions: S → A: required parts. A → M: finished goods. Each node is in a different economy; quantities and shipment times are not specified.

hug-7-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-7-6-004.title: Fixed external payments and falling export receipts
hug-7-6-004.description: Hypothetical national account in the same foreign-currency unit. Annual debt-service payments remain 20; export receipts fall from 100 to 80. No reserves, other inflows or maturity details are supplied.
hug-7-6-004.caption: Original simplified financing indicator. The payment-to-export ratio alone does not establish default, a complete sustainability judgment or an individual borrowing recommendation.
